title: 3D
heading: 3D
text: Vertex 3D stays vector-native: meshes are small JSON documents, projected every frame through a perspective camera into flat-shaded vector polygons. title: Concepts
heading: Concepts
text: One page, the whole mental model. cartridge (JSON) ──loadCartridge──▶ Game ── step() ×60/s ──▶ World ──▶ renderer / SVG / network │ ▲ input ──▶ actions systems run in order, mutate it Concept What it is Key rule --- --- --- Cartridge the game as one JSON document the only source of truth World shapes, entities, state , timers, camera everything that matters lives here Entity a plain object: transform, velocity, tags , data , optional body / emitter / interact tags decide what touches it Shape vector art: SVG path(s), or a 3D mesh pivot at (0, 0), rotation 0 faces +x, y down System a step funct

title: Concepts
heading: Determinism
text: Same cartridge + seed + inputs ⇒ same frames, byte for byte. That's what makes replays, rewind, tests and lockstep work. Keep it by: using random() / rand() / hash() / noise() for randomness, keeping all state in the world, and never reading the clock in game logic.

title: Concepts
heading: Frames are text
text: toSVG() renders the world as a canonical SVG string; digest() hashes it. Agents read frames as text, tests compare digests, and two runtimes (JS, Python) agree on them exactly.

title: Concepts
heading: Multiplayer
text: The server runs the same Game . Each player is an entity with data.player ; rules running for that entity read that player's input. Clients receive nearby entities as deltas and draw locally. So a single-player cartridge with a multiplayer block is already a multiplayer game.

title: Concepts
heading: Glossary
text: chunk : square region of a streamed world · dormant : a sleeping chunk's saved entities · focus : entities that keep chunks awake (players) · interest : radius a client receives · HUD : state.hud text overlay · policy : a function that presses actions, for bots/tests · conformance : the test suite every runtime must match.

title: Cookbook
heading: Game flow
text: Pause with a key ( systems keep running; gate your rules): [ { "when": "pressed('pause')", "do": "state.paused = !state.paused" }, { "each": "player", "when": "!state.paused", "do": "self.x += self.vx dt" } ] Levels: put each in scenes , then goto('level2') . Restart: goto(state.scene) . High score that survives restarts: keep it in top-level state (scenes merge, they don't reset).

title: Cookbook

text: Line of sight: "when": "raycast(self.x, self.y, p.x - self.x, p.y - self.y, dist(self, p), 'wall') == null" (with let p = first('player') earlier in do , or a when on a per-step rule). Procedural chunk content (needs streaming ): { "on": "chunkEnter", "when": "event.fresh", "do": "repeat (8) { let x = event.x + hash(event.cx, event.cy, i) event.size; let y = event.y + hash(event.cx, event.cy, 100 + i) event.size; if (noise(x / 200, y / 200, 1) > 0.5) spawn('tree', {x: x, y: y, body: {static: true}}) }" }

Floating text: spawn(null, {text: '+10', size: 10, x: b.x, y: b.y, vy: -30, stroke: ' ffd166', data: {ttl: 0.8}}) . title: Multiplayer and MMO servers
heading: Multiplayer and MMO servers
text: Any cartridge can be served to many players. The server runs the authoritative simulation; clients send only input and receive what is near them. npx vertex serve game.json --port 8080 --root .

title: Multiplayer and MMO servers
heading: Make a cartridge multiplayer
text: Add a multiplayer block. Your single-player rules usually need no changes: "multiplayer": { "player": { "shape": "hero", "tags": ["player"], "body": {}, "data": { "gold": 0 } }, // each joiner "spawn": { "x": 160, "y": 160, "spread": 60 }, "interest": 480, // each client receives only entities within this radius "publicData": ["name", "hp"], // data keys other players can see (own player sees everything) "sendRate": 20 // snapshots per second } How existing rules keep working: each player gets an id ( p1 , p2 , …) and an entity with data.player . When a rule runs for that entity ( each → self

title: Multiplayer and MMO servers
heading: Scale
text: - Interest management : clients only receive entities within interest of their player. - Deltas : only changed fields are sent; unchanged entities cost nothing. - Shared encoding : each entity's change is encoded once per tick and reused for every client. - Dead reckoning : moving things are re-sent only when they deviate from their predicted path ( epsilon , default 0.5 units) or change velocity. Clients integrate velocities between snapshots. - Client-side cosmetics : particles never cross the network; clients run emitters locally. - Streaming : with streaming , only chunks near players are

title: Multiplayer and MMO servers
heading: Embedding the server
text: import { serve, GameServer } from 'vertex-engine/node'; const { url, server, stop } = await serve({ cartridge, port: 8080, root: 'public' }); // or bring your own transport (anything with send(text) and on('message' 'close')) const game = new GameServer(cartridge, { seed: 1, fps: 30 }); wss.on('connection', (socket) => game.connect(adapt(socket))); setInterval(() => game.step(), 1000 / 30); Clients: createPlayer({ canvas, server: 'wss://host/ws' }) or the lower-level NetClient.connect(url) which you can drive with bindKeys , touchControls , etc.

title: Multiplayer and MMO servers
heading: Limits (honest)
text: - No client-side prediction of the local player yet: input round-trips (~1 RTT + up to one snapshot interval). Fine for exploration, social and RPG games; fast twitch shooters will feel latency. - No built-in persistence or accounts: save server.game.saveState() / per-player data yourself. - No lag compensation or anti-cheat beyond server authority and input validation. - One process simulates one world; sharding across processes is up to you.

title: The Vertex way
heading: The Vertex way
text: Vertex is an extremely opinionated framework for games made of text , with a plain library underneath. Each opinion removes a class of work and has a cost: Opinion You get You give up --- --- --- Everything is a vector (SVG paths, meshes, stroke font) KB-sized games, any resolution, art that people and models can edit bitmaps, textures, painterly art Text is the source of truth (one JSON cartridge) diffs, forks, games as links, AI-authored games opaque editor-only workflows The simulation is deterministic few-KB replays, rewind, exact bug reports, tests, lockstep, a bit-identical Python runtim

title: The Vertex way
heading: Three layers
text: Layer You write Use when --- --- --- Cartridge (framework) JSON: shapes, entities, systems, rules almost always JS systems (game, dt) => { … } next to a cartridge logic rules can't express Library your own loop, using World , Game , renderers, server… embedding Vertex in another app JS systems can break determinism and the state-in-the-world rule. Don't, unless you've decided replays and rewind don't matter for your game.

title: The Vertex way
heading: Not a fit
text: Photoreal or texture-heavy art · depth-buffered 3D with shadows or skeletal animation · a visual editor as the main workflow · competitive twitch netcode (see [multiplayer limits](multiplayer.md limits-honest)).

title: Rules reference
heading: Rule kinds
text: Rules run in array order, once per step, where "rules" sits in systems . Rule Runs Binds --- --- --- { do } every step — { each: tag, do } once per entity with tag self { on: "start", do } first step only — { on: "hit", tags?: [a, b], do } per hit event so far this step, matching tag order a , b , event { on: "contact", tags?: [a, b], do } per physics contact , tags in either order a (has tag a), b , event { on: "<type>", do } per event of that type so far this step event Any rule may add when: "<expression>" ; do is a string or an array of strings (joined by ; ).

title: Systems reference
heading: Systems reference
text: "systems" is the game loop, run in order every step. Events reach only systems listed after the one that emits them, so "rules" usually goes after collide / physics . System Does Emits --- --- --- "rules" runs the cartridge's [rules](rules.md) (at most once in the list) your events "motion" x += vx·dt , y += vy·dt , rot += vr·dt ; applies drag "wrap" entities tagged wrap re-enter from the opposite edge "lifetime" counts down data.ttl , despawns at 0 { "collide": [[a, b], …] } bounding-circle overlap between tag pairs hit { "collideOutline": [[a, b], …] } exact outline overlap hit "physics" gr

title: Troubleshooting
heading: Troubleshooting
text: Symptom Cause Fix --- --- --- hit / contact rules never run "rules" is before collide / physics in systems move "rules" after them on: "scene" / "join" rule doesn't fire on that step these events arrive at the start of the next step expected; act in the handler Replay says MISMATCH nondeterminism: Math.random() , clock, state kept in a JS closure, or a different seed/fps use game.random() ; keep state in world ; record seed and fps Rewind ( R ) jumps to wrong state a JS system keeps private state between steps store it in entity.data or world.state Value becomes NaN field was never set: undef

title: Tutorial
heading: Tutorial

heading: Endless worlds with streaming
text: "streaming": { "chunk": 320, "radius": 1, "focus": "player" }, "systems": ["streaming", "rules", "motion", ...] Only chunks within radius of a focus entity are awake. Everything else sleeps as JSON in world.dormant and wakes exactly as it was. Memory and CPU follow the number of players, not the size of the world. You have {actor.data.gold} gold.", "choices": [ { "text": "Buy (10 gold)", "when": "actor.data.gold >= 10", "do": "actor.data.gold -= 10; actor.data.sword = true", "goto": "sold" }, { "text": "Tell me about the mountain", "goto": "lore" }, { "text": "Bye", "goto": null } ] }, "lore": { "speaker": "{npc.data.name}", "text": "Long story.\nVery long.", "next": "hi" }, "sold": { "text": "Mind the edge.", "next": null } } } } - {expr} interpolates rules expressions; npc is who you talk to

title: Huge worlds, dialogue and interactions
heading: Interactions
text: { "shape": "npc", "x": 300, "y": 200, "data": { "name": "Ilka" }, "interact": { "prompt": "Talk", "dialogue": "smith", "radius": 40 } } { "shape": "lever", "x": 500, "y": 200, "interact": { "prompt": "Pull", "do": "state.gate = true; self.rot = 0.6", "once": true } } The nearest interactable within radius of each player shows a prompt; the interact action (key, gamepad button, or tapping the prompt) starts its dialogue or runs do with self and actor bound. On touch devices the player shows on-screen buttons for every action the cartridge binds, plus an analog joystick. See examples/frontier/fr
